question.leadin: The Rashidun caliphate spread Islam throughout much of the Middle East.
question.text: The caliphate was mostly composed of tribes of this ethnic group. Egypt, Iraq, and Algeria have large populations of this ethnic group, for which the peninsula containing Oman and Yemen is also named.
question.clue: These people fought on both sides of the Battle of Badr and conquered the Sassanid Empire.

swap.leadin: The Balfour Declaration supported the creation of a "national home" for members of a certain religion, which became this country.
swap.text: Name this country that was invaded by five Arab nations shortly after its creation in 1948.
swap.clue: Along with Lehi , another paramilitary group carried out the Deir Yassin massacre in this modern-day country, although the Haganah criticized them for violating this country's "purity of arms" policy.

question.text: This Islamic political organization was suppressed during Mubarak's time in office, but formed the Freedom and Justice Party to contest elections after Mubarak's resignation.
question.answerHtml: Muslim Brotherhood (accept The Society of the Muslim Brothers)
question.clue: Its first meeting place was created in Ismailia by its founder Hassan al-Bannah ("HAH-sen al-buh-NAH").

swap.leadin: In the weeks after this man was overthrown in a July 3, 2013 military coup, he was said to be in a "safe place" but had not made a public appearance.
swap.text: Name this former President of the Muslim Brotherhood's political party, the Freedom and Justice Party, who was elected President of his nation in 2012, shortly after the downfall of Hosni Mubarak.
swap.clue: This leader defeated the Salafist Nour party to win his first election.

question.text: The earlier Cossack rebel Stenka Razin was raiding Russia, got distracted, and went for a pillage in this modern-day country instead. The Safavid Empire was centered in this modern-day country.
question.clue: This country was led by Mohammad Mosaddegh, and this nation's Qajar dynasty was replaced by its Pahlavi dynasty.

swap.text: Levi Eshkol, who led Israel during the Six-Day War, was the successor to this prime minister of Israel. This prime minister briefly resigned after the Lavon Affair.
swap.clue: This man increased his nation's population via Operation Magic Carpet, which flew in almost fifty thousand Yemenis "On Wings of Angels".

question.text: This dynasty replaced the Fatimids in Egypt. It was led by its namesake's Kurdish son Saladin.
question.clue: This dynasty lost territory under al-Adil and al-Kamil, and was finally driven out of its chief territory following the Battle of al-Mansurah.

swap.text: The Safavid conversion to the Twelver sect of this branch of Islam is the major reason for its prevalence in Iran today. This smaller of the two major branches of Islam holds that Muhammad's rightful successor was Ali.
swap.clue: This denomination was the official religion of the Safavid Empire. Shah Abbas the Great enforced the Twelver sect of this denomination throughout the majority of modern Iran, where it remains the majority today above Sunni Islam.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Hadramawt diaspora.
question.text: The diaspora originated in this present-day country, whose Hadramawt governorate administers the island of Socotra.
question.clue: Muhammad al-Badr was deposed as king of its Mutawakkilite Kingdom provoking a 1962 Civil War.

swap.text: One major goal of the Ottoman government in the nineteenth century was the settlement of this mostly nomadic people in Eastern Anatolia. They briefly formed an independent principality under 'Ubaydallah in 1880 and came into bloody conflict with Armenian farmers.
swap.clue: 1991 no-fly zones protected Shias and refugees of this ethnicity, who were killed with mustard gas in Halabja ("huh-lob-ZEH") during the Anfal genocide led by Ba'athists.

question.leadin: During this war, humans surrendered to a drone for the first time in human history.
question.text: Name this war that also saw the final deployment of battleships in a combat role. The losing side in this war set fire to the oil wells of a nation that had earlier been accused of slant drilling.
question.clue: A Las Vegas conference in this war's aftermath led to the Tailhook sexual assault scandal.

swap.leadin: This battle is commemorated by the holiday of Ashura, which is celebrated during the month of Muharram.
swap.text: Name this 680 AD battle in which a small force led by Muhammad's grandson Husayn was wiped out in Iraq. It triggered the Second Fitna, or Islamic civil war.
swap.clue: Prior to this battle, the governor of Al-Basrah was sent by Yazid I to warn tribal leaders of reprisal if they fail to keep order among their people.

question.text: The Banu Musa brothers worked alongside this scholar, who translated the Roman cartography treatise Geography into Arabic. Another treatise by this scholar introduced Indian numerals to the Arabic world.

swap.text: This caliph sent the general Amr ibn al-'As to capture that fortress at Babylon, whereupon he founded Fustat. This caliph, who succeeded Abu Bakr and preceded Uthman, was given the title al-Farooq by Muhammad.
swap.clue: The last Sassanian king, Yazdegird III, was murdered by a brigand after his forces were defeated by this caliph's force at Qadisiyya. His creation of the qadi judgeship and divan pension system is considered the beginning of Islamic jurisprudence.

question.text: This Zionist paramilitary organization murdered British police officer Ralph Cairns in response to the White Paper. This organization split off from the more moderate Haganah and carried out the King David Hotel bombing.
question.clue: This group received weapons and training from the Polish army thanks to the political influence of Ze'ev Jabotinsky and, along with the Stern Gang, committed the Deir Yassin massacre.

swap.leadin: It has been speculated that John Damascene worked as an official for this dynasty, and his father Sergius was apparently head of this government's treasury for nearly 50 years.
swap.text: Name this dynasty, founded by Mu'awiya I. This dynasty was challenged during the Second Fitna, which ended with the death of Ibn al-Zubayr at the Siege of Mecca.
swap.clue: Abu Muslim's revolt against Marwan II ended this dynasty at the Battle of the Zab River.

question.leadin: This commander originally fought against and defeated Muhammed at the Battle of Uhud, but after his conversion led the Muslims to victory at Mu'Tah and Taif.
question.text: Identify this brilliant Arab General, known as "The Sword of Allah," who destroyed the Sassanid empire in Mesopotamia, ended the Riddah wars, conquered most of Syria, and did it all while being spectacularly outnumbered in almost every battle.
question.clue: This man was officially dismissed from his command for bestowing a large sum of money on the poet Ash'as for a poem praising his deeds.

swap.leadin: This ruler's envoy Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas visited China and attempted to convert Emperor Gaozong.
swap.text: Name this third caliph who convened the committee that would decide on the text of the Qu'ran and succeeded Umar.
swap.clue: This man's general and brother, Abdullah ibn Saad, killed Gregory the Patrician, exarch of Africa, and defeated a Byzantine fleet at the Battle of the Masts, and his defeat of Yazdegerd III ended the Sassanian dynasty in Persia.

question.leadin: This mystic famously declared "I am the Truth," prompting allegations that he claimed to be divine.
question.text: Name this mystic who was crucified by the Abbasid Caliph Al-Muqtadir in 922.

swap.text: 'Arib claimed to have been born into this family of Iranian nobles, who were originally a group of Buddhist leaders in Balkh. Under the Abbasids, this family became a dynasty of viziers, starting with its member Khalid.
swap.clue: Harun also destroyed the power of this family after one of its members impregnated his sister Abassa. This family patronized scholars such as Geber and was influential during the early years of the caliphate.
